:::{#exm-conditioning-reduces-entropy}
#### Learning a noisy copy lowers the entropy
<!-- no-figure: the example reports a handful of numbers, with nothing to plot -->

For the coin $X$ and noisy copy $Y$ in @exm-mutual-information-noisy-copy,
the [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) of $Y$ is $1$ [bit](#def-bit).
Given $X$, the variable $Y$ is a coin with [probabilities](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $0.8$ and $0.2$.
The chunk computes the [conditional entropy](#def-conditional-entropy) from that coin.

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
h_y <- 1
h_y_given_x <- -0.8 * log2(0.8) - 0.2 * log2(0.2)
c(h_y = h_y, h_y_given_x = h_y_given_x)
```

Here $\entropyf{Y \mid X} = `r round(h_y_given_x, 3)`$ [bits](#def-bit),
which is below $\entropyf{Y} = `r h_y`$ bit (@cor-conditioning-reduces-entropy).

:::
